item.title: Citi / AAdvantage Executive vs. Globe: 2 great options for American Airlines fans
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.33
Citi / AAdvantage Executive vs. Globe: 2 great options for American Airlines fans Editor's Note The Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® (see rates and fees) and Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) are closely-competing cards aimed at American Airlines enthusiasts. Their annual fees — $350 and $695, respectively — are far enough apart to make it important to carefully consider which option is best for you. If you're going to spend an extra $345 each year on a card, you want to make sure you're getting at least as much value as you're paying for. You should get the AAdvantage Globe if you often fly American but aren't loyal to the airline, while the AAdvantage Executive is at its most powerful in the hands of a dedicated American Airlines loyalist. Since both cards earn AAdvantage miles, offer some level of Admirals Club access and provide day-of-travel perks for American Airlines, we'll need to dig deep into the details to highlight why each card fits specific types of travelers. AAdvantage Executive vs. AAdvantage Globe: At a glance | Card Features | AAdvantage Executive | AAdvantage Globe | |---|---|---| | Annual fee | $695 | $350 | | Welcome offer | For a limited time, earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months of account opening. | Earn 60,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months of account opening. | | Authorized user fee | $175 for the first three authorized users, then $175 per authorized user | $0 | Quick picks by traveler type | Best for | Card | |---|---| | American Airlines loyalists | AAdvantage Executive | | Travelers who want to access Oneworld partner lounges | AAdvantage Executive | | Travelers who fly with American Airlines often but not exclusively | AAdvantage Globe | | Those who don't visit Admirals Clubs more than four times per year | AAdvantage Globe | AAdvantage Executive vs. AAdvantage Globe: Welcome bonus For a limited time, new Citi / AAdvantage Executive cardholders can earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months of account opening. According to TPG's September 2026 valuations, these bonus miles are worth $1,813. This is the highest-ever offer we've seen on this card, so now is a great time to apply. On the other side, the Citi / AAdvantage Globe offers a welcome bonus of 60,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months of account opening. According to TPG's valuations, these bonus miles are worth $870. This is a fairly standard offer for this card, so we recommend waiting for a better one. Keep in mind that you won't be eligible for one of these welcome bonuses if you earned one on the same card in the past 48 months. That includes any card that you earned a welcome bonus on in the past 48 months and then converted to either the Globe or Executive. Winner: AAdvantage Executive. Its welcome bonus is worth almost $1,000 more, but note that the spending requirement is much steeper. AAdvantage Executive vs. AAdvantage Globe: Benefits The AAdvantage Executive and AAdvantage Globe share many benefits, but there are key differences in statement credits and lounge access to consider. | Card name | AAdvantage Executive | AAdvantage Globe | |---|---|---| | Lounge access | Complimentary Admirals Club membership | Four Admirals Club one-time-use passes each year | | Other day-of-travel perks | | | | Statement credits | | | Day-of-travel perks are fairly similar between the two cards. If you're someone who likes to board the plane as early as possible, you'll find a lot to appreciate in the Executive's Group 4 boarding versus the Globe's Group 5. Ultimately, I believe the biggest question about the benefits of these two cards is lounge access. If you only visit Admirals Club lounges a handful of times each year, you likely won't see the point in paying a few hundred dollars extra for a full-fledged Admirals Club membership. However, if you frequent Oneworld partner lounges or fly through airports with Admirals Clubs five times or more each year, there's real value to be had from the Executive's complimentary Admirals Club membership. Getting a membership through the Executive is almost $1,000 cheaper than paying for a separate Admirals Club membership. Provided you maximize the Citi / AAdvantage Globe's annual Splurge credit and use all four of the card's Admirals Club day passes, you'll be $66 in the positive against its $350 annual fee. That's great news for those who don't like to check bags, but travelers who fly with a checked bag can save even more on domestic American Airlines flights thanks to the Globe's free first checked bag perk. The Citi / AAdvantage Executive's statement credits will likely be harder for travelers to use compared to the Globe's, since the bulk of their value comes from American Airlines Vacations purchases, inflight spending and Lyft rides. Since you have to take three Lyft rides in a month to qualify for one $15 credit, I don't consider this credit particularly valuable relative to the Executive's annual fee. Winner: Tie. The AAdvantage Executive provides significant value for those who can take advantage of a full Admirals Club membership, while the AAdvantage Globe's statement credits will likely be a lot easier to use. How to earn and redeem rewards with the AAdvantage Executive vs. AAdvantage Globe These two cards have different goals regarding their earning rates. The AAdvantage Executive stays focused on the AAdvantage ecosystem, while the Globe centers more on everyday spending. | Card name | AAdvantage Executive | AAdvantage Globe | |---|---|---| | Earning rates | | | The Citi / AAdvantage Executive earns only 1 point per dollar spent more than the Citi / AAdvantage Globe on American Airlines purchases (unless you spend $150,000 or more on your card in a year). That's not a meaningful difference, given the notable gap between the two cards' annual fees. The AAdvantage Globe is the way to go if you're looking for an AAdvantage card for your everyday spending, as it offers more bonus categories than the Executive card. I generally recommend putting airline spending only on a cobranded airline card, since you'll typically get more value by earning transferable rewards on your other purchases. The only exceptions are if your airline card is your only card or you're trying to stack up airline miles. Both cards earn 1 Loyalty Point per dollar spent, but the AAdvantage Executive is better for chasing status. You'll receive a 10,000-Loyalty Point boost after reaching four different thresholds in the same status qualification year, while the Globe provides 5,000 Loyalty Points for every four qualifying American Airlines flights (up to 15,000 bonus Loyalty Points each year). When it comes to redeeming your rewards, both cards offer the same redemption options. Neither card offers a bonus for certain redemptions that the other doesn't. TPG's managing editor for credit cards, Giselle Gomez, recently used 16,000 AAdvantage miles to book a round-trip flight between Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) and Miami International Airport (MIA) for her husband and son. Winner: The Globe if you're only concerned about earning the most miles on your non-AA purchases; those chasing status will prefer the Executive. Can I have both the AAdvantage Executive and AAdvantage Globe? Yes. However, I don't see much reason to hold both cards unless you anticipate maximizing the statement credits and bonus categories on both. Holding both cards means you'll be eligible for two separate welcome offers. That may be appealing to some, especially those looking to rack up a ton of AAdvantage miles in a short amount of time. Just make sure you plan your applications accordingly so you can hit the spending requirements on both cards. Should I get the AAdvantage Executive or AAdvantage Globe? The Citi / AAdvantage Executive is your best option if you anticipate visiting a lot of Admirals Club lounges each year or are chasing AAdvantage status. Otherwise, the Citi / AAdvantage Globe is likely sufficient for you. Upgrading or downgrading between the AAdvantage Executive and AAdvantage Globe If you already have one of these cards and want to switch to the other, call the number on the back of your card. Just keep in mind that you won't be eligible to earn a welcome bonus on the card you're switching to. Bottom line Either the AAdvantage Executive or AAdvantage Globe can make a great choice for an American Airlines enthusiast. Just make sure you carefully consider which card's benefits are a better fit for you, since they both charge annual fees in the hundreds. I recommend the Executive if you're a frequent Admirals Club visitor or chasing AAdvantage status. Conversely, go for the Globe if you're interested in earning the most AAdvantage miles on the widest range of purchases or you want statement credits that are easier to maximize. To learn more, check out our full review of the AAdvantage Executive and our full review of the AAdvantage Globe. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Globe Mastercard
